result.summary: 本文提出了“精度感知”的缩放定律，用于预测语言模型在低精度训练和后训练量化下的损失 [abstract]。作者提出低精度训练会降低模型的有效参数量，并据此预测低精度训练和后训练量化带来的额外损失 [abstract]。对于推理，后训练量化带来的退化随训练数据增加而增大，最终使额外的预训练数据变得有害 [abstract]。作者在超过 465 次预训练运行上拟合，并在最多 1.7B 参数、最多 26B token 的模型上验证了预测 [abstract]。

research_question.text: 论文要解决的问题是：精度、参数量和数据之间存在怎样的权衡，以及这些权衡在预训练和推理时有何不同 [S1.p1]。原文指出，精度是同时影响成本和性能的第三个重要因素，而当前的缩放定律没有考虑这一点 [S1.p1][abstract]。

evidence.quote: However, the precision in which models are trained and served is an important third factor that contributes to both cost and performance.
What are the tradeoffs between precision, parameters, and data? How do they compare for pretraining and inference?
Low precision training and inference affect both the quality and cost of language models, but current scaling laws do not account for this.

method.text: 论文提出“精度感知”的缩放定律，核心思想是低精度训练会降低模型的有效参数量 N_eff，并将量化实现细节抽象为仅通过 N_eff 影响损失缩放 [S1.p2][abstract]。作者将 Chinchilla 缩放形式中的 N 替换为 N_eff，并假设权重、激活和 KV cache 的量化效应独立且可乘 [S4.SS1.p2][S4.SS2.p4]。对于后训练量化，作者将退化建模为随 D/N 增长的幂律项与随量化精度指数衰减项的乘积 [S3.SS1.p1]。最终将训练和推理的缩放定律统一为单一函数形式 [abstract][S5.p8]。

evidence.quote: This functional form that posits bit precision and parameter count interchangeably contribute to a model’s “effective parameter count,” $N_{\text{eff}}$, and implementation details like which parts of a model are quantized to what precision, interact with loss scaling only through their effect on this quantity.
we find the best fit for the tradeoff between weight precision and parameters is $N_{\text{eff}}(N,P_{\text{w}})=N(1-e^{-P_{\text{w}}/\gamma_{\text{w}}})$
If the effects of quantizing weights, activations, and attention are independent, then a factorized, multiplicative interaction of the following form is a natural proposal.
we model $\delta_{\text{PTQ}}$ as taking the form: $\delta_{\text{PTQ}}(N,D,P_{\text{post}})=C_{T}\left(\frac{D^{\gamma_{D}}}{N^{\gamma_{N}}}\right)e^{-P_{\text{post}}/\gamma_{\text{post}}}$
We unify the scaling laws for post and pretraining quantization to arrive at a single functional form that predicts degradation from training and inference in varied precisions.

experiments.text: 作者在 Dolma V1.7 数据集上训练和评估了一系列 OLMo 风格的模型，使用标准 Transformer++ 实现 [S2.SS3.p1]。实验覆盖 N 从 30M 到 220M 参数、D 从 1.5B 到 26B token，并对每个 (N,D) 组合进行超过 20 次运行，扫描 8 个精度值 [S2.SS3.p1][S1.p4]。训练精度扫描范围为 3 到 16 bit，并对每个模型进行多种精度的后训练量化 [S1.p4]。作者在最多 1.7B 参数、最多 26B token 的模型上验证了预测 [abstract]。

evidence.quote: We train and evaluate a suite of OLMo-style models on the Dolma V1.7 dataset, using a standard Transformer++ implementation
Our experiments consist of a sweep of language model pretraining runs over $N\in[30,60,110,220]$ million parameters (non-embedding) and $D\in[1.5,3,6,13,26]$ billion tokens.
we sweep 8 values of precision for each of the (weights, activations, attention).
we pretrain a suite of 465 language models in 3 to 16 bit precisions, as well as post-train quantize each to multiple precisions.
We fit on over 465 pretraining runs and validate our predictions on model sizes up to 1.7B parameters trained on up to 26B tokens.

findings.text: 后训练量化的损失退化随训练数据量增加而增大，对于固定模型，超过某个数据量后额外预训练数据会主动损害推理时性能 [S3.SS1.p1][S3.SS1.p2]。训练时量化权重、激活和 KV cache 的效应可建模为独立且可乘，通过有效参数量 N_eff 预测损失 [S4.SS2.p5]。当 N、D、P 联合优化时，计算最优预训练精度与计算预算无关，拟合结果约为 7-8 bit；而当 N 固定时，计算最优精度随计算量对数增长 [S4.SS3.SSS2.p1][S4.SS3.SSS3.p1]。统一缩放定律在超过 1000 个数据点上取得 R²=0.90 的拟合 [S5.p6]。

evidence.quote: We find that the degradation $\delta_{\text{PTQ}}$ increases in training data size across all model sizes, but that for a fixed dataset size larger models incur a smaller degradation.
This finding implies that for models that will be post-train quantized, there exists an amount of pretraining data beyond which additional data is actively harmful to performance at inference-time
The effects of quantizing the weights, activations, and KV cache during training are well modeled as independent and multiplicative
which reveals that in general the optimal pretraining precision is independent of compute budget.
We find this $P^{*}$ to be around 7-8 bits when fitting our scaling law on runs with quantization done to integer type.
our scaling laws predict that models of differing sizes should not necessarily be trained in the same precision, and that compute-optimal precision scales as $P^{*}(C)\propto\log C$.
We measure the fit to the data of such a functional form in Figure 7, and find a strong fit with $R^{2}=0.90$ on over 1000 data points

limitations.text: 作者承认，全文使用固定架构来考察精度、参数和 token 的影响，而低精度训练通常涉及架构调整，可以缩小与普通全精度模型的差距 [S6.p2]。其次，虽然计算成本随精度线性缩放，但由于系统开销，减半精度带来的收益通常不到 2 倍 [S6.p2]。第三，论文只考虑损失缩放，没有进行下游模型评估 [S6.p2]。作者强调所发现的趋势旨在提供启示而非规定性结论 [S6.p2]。

evidence.quote: First, we use a fixed architecture throughout to examine the effects of precision, parameters, and tokens in a controlled manner.
In contrast, low precision training often involves architectural tweaks that can close much of the gap from a vanilla full precision model.
Second, while compute costs do scale linearly with precision, the gains from halving precision are usually less than 2x due to systems overhead.
Third, we only consider loss scaling without downstream model evaluations.
We emphasize that the trends we find aim to be suggestive rather than prescriptive
